newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cuba vice president met Argentina's Menem-diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Cuba vice president met Argentina's Menem-diplomat.

text.p: Cuban Vice President Carlos Lage met secretly with Argentina's President Carlos Menem on Wednesday seeking support against U.S. trade sanctions, a Cuban diplomatic source said on Thursday.
"He came specially from Uruguay to deliver a letter from President Fidel Castro to President Carlos Menem," the source, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters in Buenos Aires.

In a diplomatic offensive begun last week, Cuban envoys have handed letters from Castro to several Latin American leaders denouncing moves in the U.S. Congress to tighten the 35-year-old trade embargo against Cuba. The measures would strengthen the Helms-Burton law, which seeks to discourage foreign investment in Cuba.

Since Menem took office in 1989, Argentina has adopted a tough stance against Cuba's communist regime, supporting demands by the Cuban exile community in the United States for political reforms on the island. But Menem joined other Latin American leaders last year in condemning the U.S. law, which punishes foreign firms investing in property seized in Cuba from U.S. citizens and companies after the 1959 revolution.
Lage met on Tuesday with Uruguayan President Julio Sanguinetti in Montevideo on a tour shrouded in secrecy.

Cuban Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina met Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Friday, Costa Rican President Jose Maria Figueres on Monday and Dominican President Leonel Fernandez on Tuesday, handing each a letter from Castro. He also visited Guatemala and Panama.
According to a copy of the letter released by Costa Rica's government, Castro lambasted the new U.S. moves against Cuba.

"These measures are aimed at reinforcing the economic, financial and commercial blockade (of Cuba), and strengthening the aggressive policies that Washington has maintained for more than 35 years against our country," Castro's letter said.
